s.d: Α, α, ἄλφα (which see), τό, indecl., alpha, the first letter of the Greek alphabet. As a numeral, ά = 1, α = 1000. As a prefix, it appears to have at least two and perhaps three distinct senses: 1. ἀ- (before a vowel, ἀν-) negative, as in ἄ-γνωστος, ἄ-δικος. 2. ἀ-, ἁ- copulative, indicating community and fellowship, as in ἁ-πλοῦς, ἀ-κολουθέω, ἀ-δελφός. 3. An intensive force (LS, s. α), as in ἀ-τενίζω is sometimes assumed (but see Boisacq, see word). (AS)
ἔα, interj., expressing surprise, indignation, fear (in cl. chiefly in poët.), ah! ha!: [[luke 4 34|Luk.4:34.]]† (AS)
Ἀαρών (Heb. אַהֲרוֹן), indecl. (in FlJ, -ῶνος), Aaron ([[exodus 4 14|Exo.4:14]], al.): [[luke 1 5|Luk.1:5]], [[acts 7 40|Act.7:40]], [[hebrews 5 4|Heb.5:4, 7:11, 9:4]].† (AS)

Ἀβαδδών (Heb. אֲבַדּוֹן, destruction; LXX, ἀπώλεια, only in Wisdom Lit., of the place of the ruined dead: [[job 26 6|Job.26:6, 28:22, 31:12]], [[psalms 88 12|Psa.88:12]], [[proverbs 15 11|Pro.15:11]]*), indecl.; in NT, Abaddon, the angel of the Abyss: [[revelation 9 11|Rev.9:11.]]† (AS)
αβαρής, -ές (βαρός), without weight; metaphorically (MM, VGT, see word) not burdensome: [[2-corinthians 11 9|2Co.11:9.]]† (AS)

Ἀββά (T, -ᾶ), indecl. (Aram, אַבָּא, emphatic form of אַב = Heb. אָב, father), used in the phrase Ἀ. ὁ παήρ, Abba, Father (see Swete on Mk, I.with): [[mark 14 36|Mrk.14:36]], [[romans 8 15|Rom.8:15]], [[galatians 4 6|Gal.4:6]].† (AS)
Ἄβελ, (WH, Ἅ-), ὁ, indecl. (הֶבֶל), Abel ([[genesis 4 2|Gen.4:2-10]]): [[hebrews 11 4|Heb.11:4, 12:24]]; αἵμα Ἄ., [[matthew 23 35|Mat.23:35]], [[luke 11 51|Luk.11:51]].† (AS)

Ἀβιά (Heb. אֲבִיָּה, אֲבִיָּהוּ), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἀβίας, -α), Abia, Abijah. 1. Son of Rehoboam (3Ki.14:1): [[matthew 1 7|Mat.1:7]]. 2. A priest of the line of Eleazar ([[1-chronicles 24 3|1Ch.24:3, 10]]): [[luke 1 5|Luk.1:5]]. † (AS)

Ἀβιά (Heb. אֲבִיָּה, אֲבִיָּהוּ), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἀβίας, -α), Abia, Abijah. 1. Son of Rehoboam (3Ki.14:1): [[matthew 1 7|Mat.1:7]]. 2. A priest of the line of Eleazar ([[1-chronicles 24 3|1Ch.24:3, 10]]): [[luke 1 5|Luk.1:5]]. † (AS)
Ἀβιάθαρ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. אֶבְיָתָר), Abiathar ([[1-kings 21 1|1Ki.21:1]]): [[mark 2 26|Mrk.2:26]].† (AS)
Ἀβειληνή (T, Rec. Ἀβι-), -ῆς, ἡ, (sc. χώρα), Abilene, a district in the Anti-Lebanon: [[luke 3 1|Luk.3:1.]]† (AS)
Ἀβιούδ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. אֲבִיָּהוּד), Abiud, Abihud: [[matthew 1 13|Mat.1:13.]]† (AS)
Ἀβραάμ (Heb. אַבְרָהָם), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἄβραμος, -ου; MM, VGT, see word), Abraham ([[genesis 17 5|Gen.17:5]] al.): [[matthew 1 1|Mat.1:1]], 2 al. (AS)

ἄ-βυσσος, -ον (Ion. βυσσός = βυθός), 1. in cl., boundless, bottomless (e.g. ἄ. πέλαγος, ἄ. πλοῦτος Æsch.). 2. [In LXX (for תְּהוֹם, [[genesis 1 2|Gen.1:2]], al.; exc. [[isaiah 44 27|Isa.44:27]], [[job 41 22|Job.41:22]] for צוּלָה, מְצוּלָה, [[job 36 16|Job.36:16]] for רַחַב) and] NT, as subst. (MM, VGT, see word), ἡ ἄ. (sc. χώρα), the abyss; (a) of the sea ([[genesis 1 2|Gen.1:2]]); (b) of the underworld, as the abode of the dead: [[romans 10 7|Rom.10:7]] (a paraphrase of [[deuteronomy 30 13|Deu.30:13]] LXX); as the abode of demons, [[luke 8 31|Luk.8:31]], [[revelation 9 1|Rev.9:1, 2, 11, 11:7, 17:8, 20:1, 3]] (Cremer, 2). † (AS)
Ἄγαβος, -ου, ὁ Agabus: [[acts 11 28|Act.11:28, 21:10]].† (AS)

ἀγαθοεργέω, -ῶ, to do good, show kindness: [[1-timothy 6 18|1 Ti 6:18]] (Cremer, 8).† ἀγαθουργέω, -ῶ, contracted form (rare, see WH, App., 145) of ἀγαθοερ- (which see), to do good: [[acts 14 17|Act.14:17.]]† (AS)

ἀγαθὀ-ποιέω, -ῶ (= cl. ἀγαθὸν ποιεῖν, εὐεργετεῖν), [in LXX: [[numbers 10 32|Num.10:32]], [[judges 17 13|Jdg.17:13]] A, [[zephaniah 1 12|Zep.1:12]] (יטב hi.), Tob.12:13 B, 1Ma.11:33, 2Ma.1:2 * ;] to do good; (a) univ.: [[1-peter 2 15|1Pe.2:15, 20, 3:6, 17, 3]]Jo.11; (b) for another's benefit: [[mark 3 4|Mrk.3:4]] (T, ἀγαθὸν ποιῆσαι), [[luke 6 9|Luk.6:9;]] (with) accusative of person(s), [[luke 6 33|Luk.6:33, 35]] (Cremer, 8). † (AS)
ἀγαθοποιία, -ας, ἡ (ἀγαθοποιός), well-doing: [[1-peter 4 19|1Pe.4:19.]]† (AS)

ἀγαθοποιός, -όν = cl. ἀγαθουργός, [in LXX, of a woman who deals pleasantly in order to corrupt, Sir.42:14 * ;] doing well, acting rightly (Plut.): [[1-peter 2 14|1Pe.2:14]] (Cremer, 8; MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

ἀγαθός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב ;] in general, good, in physical and in moral sense, used of persons, things, acts, conditions, etc., applied to that which is regarded as "perfect in its kind, so as to produce pleasure and satisfaction, . . . that which, in itself good, is also at once for the good and the advantage of him who comes in contact with it" (Cremer, 3): γῆ, [[luke 8 8|Luk.8:8;]] δένδρον, [[matthew 7 18|Mat.7:18;]] καρδία, [[luke 8 15|Luk.8:15;]] δόσις, [[james 1 17|Jas.1:17;]] μέρις, [[luke 10 42|Luk.10:42;]] ἔργον (frequently in Pl.), [[philippians 1 6|Php.1:6;]] ἐλπίς, [[2-thessalonians 2 16|2Th.2:16;]] θησαυρός, [[matthew 12 35|Mat.12:35;]] μνεία, [[1-thessalonians 3 6|1Th.3:6]] (cf. 2Ma.7:20); as subst., τὸ ἀ, that which is morally good, beneficial, acceptable to God, [[romans 12 2|Rom.12:2;]] ἐργάζεσθαι τὸ ἀ, [[romans 2 10|Rom.2:10]], [[ephesians 4 28|Eph.4:28]]; πράσσειν, [[romans 9 11|Rom.9:11]], [[2-corinthians 5 10|2Co.5:10]]; διώκειν, [[1-thessalonians 5 15|1Th.5:15;]] μιμεῖσθαι, III Jo 11; κολλᾶσθαι τῷ ἀ, [[romans 12 9|Rom.12:9;]] ερωτᾶν περὶ τοῦ ἀ., [[matthew 19 17|Mat.19:17;]] διάκονος εἰς τὸ ἀ., [[romans 13 4|Rom.13:4;]] τὸ ἀ. σου, thy favour, benefit, Phm 14; pl., τὰ ἀ., of goods, possessions, [[luke 12 18|Luk.12:18;]] of spiritual benefits, [[romans 10 15|Rom.10:15]], [[hebrews 9 11|Heb.9:11, 10:1]]. ἀ is opposite to πονηρός, [[matthew 5 45|Mat.5:45, 20:5]]; κακός, [[romans 7 19|Rom.7:19;]] φαῦλος, [[romans 9 11|Rom.9:11]], [[2-corinthians 5 10|2Co.5:10]] (cf. MM, VGT, see word). SYN.: καλός, δίκαιος. κ. properly refers to goodliness as manifested in form: ἀ. to inner excellence (cf. the cl. καλὸς κἀγαθός and ἐν καρδία κ. καὶ ἀ., [[luke 8 15|Luk.8:15]]). In [[romans 5 7|Rom.5:7]], where it is contrasted with δ., ἀ. implies a kindliness and attractiveness not necessarily possessed by the δίκαιος, who merely measures up to a high standard of rectitude (cf. ἀγαθωσύνη). (AS)

ἀγαθωσύνη (on the termination, see: ἁγιότης, and cf . WH, App., 152; MM, VGT, see word), -ης, ἡ (ἀγαθός), [in LXX for טוֹבָה, טוֹב, טוּב, only in Heb. bks. ;] goodness (representing "the kindlier, as δικαιοσύνη, the sterner element in the ideal character," AE, Eph., 5:9; on its relation to χρηστότης, see Tr., Syn., §lxiii): [[romans 15 14|Rom.15:14]], [[galatians 5 22|Gal.5:22]], [[2-thessalonians 1 11|2Th.1:11]].† (AS)

ἀγαλλίασις, -εως, ἡ (ἀγαλλιάω), [in LXX (most frequently in Pss. and often coupled with εὐφροσύνη, as [[psalms 45 15|Ps 44(45):15]]) chiefly for גִּיל ;] exultation, exuberant joy: [[luke 1 44|Luk.1:44]], [[acts 2 46|Act.2:46]], [[hebrews 1 9|Heb.1:9]], Ju 24; χαρὰ καὶ ἀ., [[luke 1 14|Luk.1:14]] (Cremer, 592).† (AS)

ἀγαλλιάω, -ῶ, Hellenistic form of cl. ἀγάλλω, to glorify, mid. -ομαι, to exult in; [in LXX (most frequently in Pss.) chiefly for גיל, רנן pi. ;] to exult, rejoice greatly: before ἐπί, with dative, [[luke 1 47|Luk.1:47;]] with dative mod., [[1-peter 1 8|1Pe.1:8]], [[revelation 19 7|Rev.19:7]]. Mid., with same sense: [[matthew 5 12|Mat.5:12]], [[luke 10 21|Luk.10:21]], [[acts 2 26|Act.2:26, 16:34]], [[1-peter 4 13|1Pe.4:13]]; before ἵνα, [[john 8 56|Jhn.8:56;]] ἐν, [[john 5 35|Jhn.5:35]] (1 aor. pass. perh. as mid.; but see Mozley, Psalter, 5), [[1-peter 1 6|1Pe.1:6]] (Cremer, 590).† (AS)
ἄ-γαμος, -ον [in LXX: 4Ma.16:9 * ;] unmarried: [[1-corinthians 7 8|1Co.7:8, 32]]; fem. (= cl. ἄνανδρος), ib. 11, 34.† (AS)

ἀγανακτέω, -ῶ (ἄγαν, much, ἄχομαι, to grieve), [in LXX: Wis.5:22, 12:27, Da TH Bel 28, 4Ma.4:21 * ;] to be indignant: [[matthew 21 15|Mat.21:15, 26:8]], [[mark 10 14|Mrk.10:14, 14:4]]; before περί, [[matthew 20 24|Mat.20:24]], [[mark 10 41|Mrk.10:41]]; before ὅτι, [[luke 13 14|Luk.13:14]] (see MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)
ἀγανάκτησις, -εως, ἡ (ἀγανακτέω), [in LXX: [[esther 18 3|Est.18:3]] א 1 * ;] indignation: [[2-corinthians 7 11|2Co.7:11]] (see MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

ἀγαπάω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for אהב ;] to love, to feel and exhibit esteem and goodwill to a person, to prize and delight in a thing. 1. Of human affection, to men: τ. πλησίον, [[matthew 5 43|Mat.5:43;]] τ. ἐχθρούς, ib. 44; to Christ, [[john 8 42|Jhn.8:42;]] to God, [[matthew 22 37|Mat.22:37;]] with accusative of thing(s), [[luke 11 43|Luk.11:43]], [[john 12 43|Jhn.12:43]], [[ephesians 5 25|Eph.5:25]], [[2-timothy 4 8|II Tim 4:8]], 10, [[hebrews 1 9|Heb.1:9]], [[1-peter 2 17|1Pe.2:17, 3:10]], [[2-peter 2 15|2Pe.2:15]], [[1-john 2 15|1Jn.2:15]], [[revelation 12 11|Rev.12:11]]. 2. Of divine love; (a) God's love: to men, [[romans 8 37|Rom.8:37;]] to Christ, [[john 3 35|Jhn.3:35;]] (b) Christ's love: to men, [[mark 10 21|Mrk.10:21;]] to God, [[john 14 31|Jhn.14:31;]] with cogn. accusative, [[john 17 26|Jhn.17:26]], [[ephesians 2 4|Eph.2:4]]. SYN.: φιλέω. From its supposed etymology (Thayer, LS; but see also Boisacq) ἀ. is commonly understood properly to denote love based on esteem (diligo), as distinct from that expressed by φιλέω (amo), spontaneous natural affection, emotional and unreasoning. If this distinction holds, ἀ. is fitly used in NT of Christian love to God and man, the spiritual affection which follows the direction of the will, and which, therefore, unlike that feeling which is instinctive and unreasoned, can be commanded as a duty. (Cf. ἀγάπη, and v. Tr., Syn. §xii; Cremer, 9, 592; and esp. MM, VGT, see word) (AS)

ἀγάπη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX for אַהֲבָה, which is also rendered by ἀγάπησις and φιλία ;] love, goodwill, esteem. Outside of bibl. and eccl. books, there is no clear instance (with Deiss., LAE, 18:4, 70:2, cf. the same writer in Constr. Quar., ii, 4; and with MM, VGT, see word, cf. Dr. Moulton in Exp. Times, xxvi, 3, 139). In NT, like ἀγαπάω, -ῶ, 1. Of men's love: (a) to one another, [[john 13 35|Jhn.13:35;]] (b) to God, [[1-john 2 5|1Jn.2:5.]] 2. Of divine love; (a) God's love: to men, [[romans 5 8|Rom.5:8;]] to Christ, [[john 17 26|Jhn.17:26;]] (b) Christ's love to men: [[romans 8 35|Rom.8:35.]] 3. In pl., love feasts: Ju 12 (DB, iii, 157). SYN.: φιλία. ἀ., signifying properly (see: ἀγαπάω) love which chooses its object, is taken over from LXX, where its connotation is more general, into NT, and there used exclusively to express that spiritual bond of love between God and man and between man and man, in Christ, which is characteristic of Christianity. It is thusdistinct from φιλία, friendship ([[james 4 4|Jas.4:4]] only), στοργή, natural affection (in NT only in compounds, see: ἄστοργος) and ἔρως, sexual love, which is not used in NT, its place being taken by ἐπιθυμία. (Cf. ἀγαπάω; and see Abbott, Essays, 70f.; DB, vol. i., 555; Cremer, 13, 593; MM, VGT, see word). (AS)

ἀγαπητός, -ή, -όν (ἀγαπάω), [in LXX chiefly for יָתִיד, יָדִיד ;] beloved (see M, Pr., 221); (a) by God: of Christ, [[matthew 3 17|Mat.3:17;]] of men, [[romans 1 7|Rom.1:7;]] (b) by Christians, of one another: [[1-corinthians 4 14|1Co.4:14;]] frequently as form of address, [[1-corinthians 10 14|ib. 10:14]]; opposite to ἐχθρός, [[romans 11 28|Rom.11:28]] (see AR, Eph., 229; Cremer, 17; MM, VGT, see word). (AS)
Ἅγαρ (Rec. Ἄ-), ἡ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἀγάρα, -ης, Heb. הָגָר), Hagar (Gen.16): [[galatians 4 24|Gal.4:24,25]].† (AS)

ἀγγαρεύω (from the Persian; cf. Vg. angiare, and the Heb. אִגֶרֶת; on the orthogr., see Bl., §6, 1; M, Pr., 46), to impress into public service, employ a courier; hence, to compel to perform a service (prob. common in the vernac.; cf. Deiss., BS, 86f., MM, Exp., iv; VGT, see word): [[matthew 5 41|Mat.5:41, 27:32]], [[mark 15 21|Mrk.15:21]].† (AS)
ἀγγεῖον, -ου, τό (ἄγγος), [in LXX chiefly for כְּלִי ;] a vessel (see MM, VGT, see word): [[matthew 25 4|Mat.25:4.]]† (AS)
ἀγγελία, -ας, ἡ (ἄγγελος), [in LXX chiefly for שְׁמוּעָה ;] a message: 1Jo.1:5, 3:11 (Cremer, 18; MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

ἄγγελος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for מַלְאָךְ ;] 1. a messenger, one sent: [[matthew 11 10|Mat.11:10]], [[james 22 25|Jas.22:25]]. 2. As in LXX, in the special sense of angel, a spiritual, heavenly being, attendant upon God and employed as his messenger to men, to make known his purposes, as [[luke 1 11|Luk.1:11]], or to execute them, as [[matthew 4 6|Mat.4:6.]] The ἄ. in [[revelation 1 20|Rev.1:20-2:1]], al., is variously understood as (1) a messenger or delegate, (2) a bishop or ruler, (3) a guardian angel, (4) the prevailing spirit of each church, i.e. the Church itself. (Cf. Swete, Ap)., in l.; DB, iv, 991; Thayer, see word; Cremer, 18; MM, VGT, see word) (AS)

ἄγγελος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for מַלְאָךְ ;] 1. a messenger, one sent: [[matthew 11 10|Mat.11:10]], [[james 22 25|Jas.22:25]]. 2. As in LXX, in the special sense of angel, a spiritual, heavenly being, attendant upon God and employed as his messenger to men, to make known his purposes, as [[luke 1 11|Luk.1:11]], or to execute them, as [[matthew 4 6|Mat.4:6.]] The ἄ. in [[revelation 1 20|Rev.1:20-2:1]], al., is variously understood as (1) a messenger or delegate, (2) a bishop or ruler, (3) a guardian angel, (4) the prevailing spirit of each church, i.e. the Church itself. (Cf. Swete, Ap)., in l.; DB, iv, 991; Thayer, see word; Cremer, 18; MM, VGT, see word) (AS)
ἄγε, prop. imperat. of ἄγω, come! used as adv. and addressed, like φέρε, to one or more persons: [[james 4 13|Jas.4:13, 5:1]].† (AS)
ἀγέλη, -ης, ἡ (ἄγω), [in LXX chiefly for עֵ֫דֶר ;] a herd: [[matthew 8 30|Mat.8:30-32]], [[mark 5 11|Mrk.5:11, 13]], [[luke 8 32|Luk.8:32,33]].† (AS)
ἀγενεαλόγητος, -ον (γενεαλογέω), without genealogy, i.e. without recorded pedigree (cf. [[nehemiah 7 64|Neh.7:64]]): [[hebrews 7 3|Heb.7:3]] (Cremer, 152; MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

ἀγενής, -ές (γένος), 1. unborn (Plat.); 2. of no family, ignoble, base (opposite to ἀγαθός, Soph., Fr., 105): opposite to εὐγενής, [[1-corinthians 1 28|1Co.1:28]] (for exx. from π., see MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

ἁγιάζω, Hellenistic form of ἁγίζω (ἅγιος), to make holy, consecrate, sanctify; [in LXX chiefly for קדשׁ pi., hi. ;] 1. to dedicate, separate, set apart for God; of things: [[matthew 23 17|Mat.23:17,19]], [[2-timothy 2 21|2Ti.2:21]]; of persons: Christ, [[john 10 36|Jhn.10:36, 17:19]]. 2. to purify, make conformable in character to such dedication: forensically, to free from guilt, [[1-corinthians 6 11|1Co.6:11]], [[ephesians 5 26|Eph.5:26]], [[hebrews 2 11|Heb.2:11, 10:10, 14, 29, 13:12]]; internally, by actual sanctification of life, [[john 17 17|Jhn.17:17, 19]], [[acts 20 32|Act.20:32, 26:18]], [[romans 15 16|Rom.15:16]], [[1-corinthians 1 2|1Co.1:2, 7:14]], [[1-thessalonians 5 23|1Th.5:23]], [[revelation 22 11|Rev.22:11]]; of a nonbeliever influenced by marriage with a Christian, [[1-corinthians 7 14|1Co.7:14.]] 3. In the intermediate sense of ceremonial or levitical purification: (a) of things, [[2-timothy 2 21|2Ti.2:21;]] (b) of persons, [[hebrews 9 13|Heb.9:13.]] 4. to treat as holy: [[matthew 6 9|Mat.6:9]], [[luke 11 2|Luk.11:2]], [[1-peter 3 16|1Pe.3:16]] (Cremer, 53, 602; MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

ἁγιασμός, -οῦ, ὁ (ἁγιάζω), [in LXX: [[ezekiel 45 4|Eze.45:4]] (מִקְדָּשׁ), Sir.7:31, etc. ;] as an active verbal noun in -μός, it signifies properly the process τὸ ἁγιάζειν, rather than the resultant state, ἁγιωσύνη, hence, 1. consecration; 2. sanctification: so strictly in [[romans 6 19|Rom.6:19,22]] (but see Meyer), [[1-corinthians 1 30|1Co.1:30]], [[1-thessalonians 4 3|1Th.4:3]],7, [[2-thessalonians 2 13|2Th.2:13]], [[hebrews 12 14|Heb.12:14]], [[1-peter 1 2|1Pe.1:2]]. Elsewhere it perhaps (Ellic.; but see Milligan, Th., 48) inclines to the resultant state: [[1-thessalonians 4 4|1Th.4:4]], [[1-timothy 2 15|1Ti.2:15]] (Cremer, 55, 602). † (AS)

ἅγιος, -α, ον (τό ἅγός, religious awe; ἅζω, to venerate), [in LXX chiefly for קֹ֫דֶשׁ ;] primarily, dedicated to the gods, sacred (Hdt.; rare in Att., never in Hom., Hes. and Trag., who use ἁγνός), hence, holy, characteristic of God, separated to God, worthy of veneration. 1. Its highest application is to God himself, in his purity, majesty, and glory: [[luke 1 49|Luk.1:49]], [[john 17 11|Jhn.17:11]], [[revelation 4 8|Rev.4:8]]. Hence (a) of things and places which have a claim to reverence as sacred to God, e.g. the Temple: [[matthew 24 15|Mat.24:15]], [[hebrews 9 1|Heb.9:1]]; (b) of persons employed by him, as angels: [[1-thessalonians 3 13|1Th.3:13;]] prophets, [[luke 1 70|Luk.1:70;]] apostles, [[ephesians 3 5|Eph.3:5.]] 2. Applied to persons as separated to God's service: (a) of Christ, [[mark 1 24|Mrk.1:24]], [[john 6 69|Jhn.6:69]], [[acts 4 30|Act.4:30]]; (b) of Christians, [[acts 9 13|Act.9:13]], [[romans 1 7|Rom.1:7]], [[hebrews 6 10|Heb.6:10]], [[revelation 5 8|Rev.5:8]]. 3. In the moral sense of sharing God's purity: [[mark 6 20|Mrk.6:20]], [[john 17 11|Jhn.17:11]], [[acts 3 14|Act.3:14]], [[revelation 3 7|Rev.3:7]]. 4. Of pure, clean sacrifices and offerings: [[1-corinthians 7 14|1Co.7:14]], [[ephesians 1 4|Eph.1:4]]. SYN.: ἁγνός, pure, both in ceremonial and spiritual sense; ἱερός (sacer), sacred, that which is inviolable because of its (external) relation to God; ὅσιος (sanctus as opposite to nefas), that which is based on everlasting ordinances of right. (Cf. Tr., Syn., §lxxxviii; DB, ii, 399 f.; Cremer, 34, 594-601; MM, VGT, see word) (AS)

ἅγιος, -α, ον (τό ἅγός, religious awe; ἅζω, to venerate), [in LXX chiefly for קֹ֫דֶשׁ ;] primarily, dedicated to the gods, sacred (Hdt.; rare in Att., never in Hom., Hes. and Trag., who use ἁγνός), hence, holy, characteristic of God, separated to God, worthy of veneration. 1. ἀδήλως (ἄδηλος), adv. uncertainly: of direction, [[1-corinthians 9 26|1Co.9:26.]]† (AS)

ἀδημονέω, -ῶ (on the derivation, see MM, VGT, see word), [in Aq.: [[job 18 20|Job.18:20;]] Sm.: Psa.60 (61):3 115:2 (116:11), [[ecclesiastes 7 17|Ecc.7:17]](16), [[ezekiel 3 15|Eze.3:15]] * ;] to be troubled, distressed (MM, l.with): [[matthew 26 37|Mat.26:37]], [[mark 14 33|Mrk.14:33]], [[philippians 2 26|Php.2:26]].† (AS)

ᾅδης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX ehiefly for שְׁאוֹל, also for דּוּמָה, מָוֶת, etc. ;] 1. in Hom., Hades (Pluto), the god of the underworld. 2. the abode of Hades, the underivorld; in NT, the abode of departed spirits, Hades: ἐν τ. ᾅ., [[luke 16 23|Luk.16:23;]] εἰς ᾅ., [[acts 2 27|Act.2:27,31]]; πύλαι ᾅδου, [[matthew 16 18|Mat.16:18;]] κλεῖς τοῦ ᾅ., [[revelation 1 18|Rev.1:18;]] metaphorically, ἕως ᾅ., [[matthew 11 23|Mat.11:23]], [[luke 10 15|Luk.10:15]]; personified, [[revelation 6 8|Rev.6:8 20:13,14]] (Cremer, 67, 610; MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

ἀ-διά-κριτος, -ον (διακρίνω), [in LXX: [[proverbs 25 1|Pro.25:1]] * ;] 1. not to be parted, mixed, undistinguishable (cf. Pr, l.with, and see Lft., Ignat. Eph., §3). 2. without uncertainty (Hort, in l., but see MM, VGT, see word): [[james 3 17|Jas.3:17.]] † (AS)
ἀδιάλειπτος, -ον (διαλείπω), unremitting, incessant: [[romans 9 2|Rom.9:2]], [[2-timothy 1 3|2Ti.1:3]]. (For exx., see MM, VGT, see word) † (AS)
ἀδιαλείπτως (see supr.), adv., [in LXX: 1Ma.12:11, II Mac .4, 3Ma.6:33 * ;] unremittingly, incessantly: [[romans 1 9|Rom.1:9]], [[1-thessalonians 1 3|1Th.1:3 2:13 5:17]].† (AS)
incorruption, uprightness , (New Testament) (ML)

ἀδικέω, -ῶ (ἄδικος), [in LXX for עשׁק, עוה, etc. ;] 1. intrans., to be ἄδικος, do wrong, act wickedly or criminally: [[acts 25 11|Act.25:11]], [[1-corinthians 6 8|1Co.6:8]], [[2-corinthians 7 12|2Co.7:12]], [[colossians 3 25|Col.3:25]], [[revelation 22 11|Rev.22:11]]; to do hurt, [[revelation 9 19|Rev.9:19.]] 2. Trans. (a) to do some wrong: ὃ ἠδίκησεν, [[colossians 3 25|Col.3:25;]] to wrong some one, [[matthew 20 13|Mat.20:13]], [[acts 7 26|Act.7:26, 27 25:10]], [[2-corinthians 7 2|2Co.7:2]], [[galatians 4 12|Gal.4:12]], Phm 18, [[2-peter 2 13|2Pe.2:13]]; pass., [[acts 7 24|Act.7:24]], [[2-corinthians 7 12|2Co.7:12]]; mid., [[1-corinthians 6 7|1Co.6:7]] (suffer . . . to be wronged; WM, §38, 3; but see Bl., §54, 5; and cf. ἀποστερέω); (b) to injure, hurt: [[luke 10 19|Luk.10:19]] [[revelation 2 11|Rev.2:11 6:6 7:2, 3 9:4,10 11:5]]. † (AS)
ἀδίκημα, -τος, τό (ἀδικέω), [in LXX for עָוֹן, פֶּשַׁע, etc. ;] a wrong, injury, misdeed (MM, VGT, see word): [[acts 18 14|Act.18:14 24:20]], [[revelation 18 5|Rev.18:5]].† (AS)

ἀδικία, -ας, ἡ (ἄδικος), [in LXX for עָוֹן, פֶּשַׁע, עָוֶל, etc. ;] 1. injustice: [[luke 18 6|Luk.18:6]], [[romans 9 14|Rom.9:14]]. 2. unrighteousness, iniquity: [[john 7 18|Jhn.7:18]], [[acts 8 23|Act.8:23]], [[romans 1 18|Rom.1:18, 29 2:8 6:13]], [[2-timothy 2 19|2Ti.2:19]], [[1-john 1 9|1Jn.1:9 5:17]]; opposite to ἀλήθεια, [[1-corinthians 13 6|1Co.13:6]], [[2-thessalonians 2 12|2Th.2:12]]; to δικαιοσύνη ], [[romans 3 5|Rom.3:5;]] ἀπάτη τῆς ἀ., [[2-thessalonians 2 10|2Th.2:10;]] μισθὸς ἀδικίας, [[acts 1 18|Act.1:18]], [[2-peter 2 13|2Pe.2:13,15]]; ἐγράται τῆς ἀ., [[luke 13 27|Luk.13:27;]] μαμωνᾶς τῆς ἀ., [[luke 16 9|Luk.16:9;]] κόσμος τῆς ἀ., [[james 3 6|Jas.3:6;]] οἰκονόμος τῆς ἀ., [[luke 16 8|Luk.16:8.]] 3. = ἀδίκημα, an unrighteous act: ironically, a favour, [[2-corinthians 12 13|2Co.12:13;]] pl., [[hebrews 8 12|Heb.8:12]] (Cremer, 261; MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

ἄδικος, -ον (δίκη), [in LXX for שׁקר, עול, etc. ;] 1. unjust: [[romans 3 5|Rom.3:5]], [[hebrews 6 10|Heb.6:10]]. 2. unrighteous, wicked: [[luke 16 11|Luk.16:11 18:11]], [[acts 24 15|Act.24:15]], [[1-corinthians 6 1|1Co.6:1]],9 [[1-peter 3 18|1Pe.3:18]]; opposite to δίκαιος, [[matthew 5 45|Mat.5:45;]] to εὐσεβής, [[2-peter 2 9|2Pe.2:9;]] to πιστός, [[luke 16 10|Luk.16:10]] (Cremer, 200). † (AS)
ἀδίκως, adv. (ἄδικος), [in LXX for שׁקר, עול, etc. ;] unjustly, undeservedly: [[1-peter 2 19|1Pe.2:19.]]† (AS)

ἀ-δόκιμος, -ον, [in LXX: [[proverbs 25 4|Pro.25:4]], [[isaiah 1 22|Isa.1:22]] (סִיג) * ;] 1. of things (prop. of metals: LXX, ll. with), not standing the test, rejected: γῆ, [[hebrews 6 8|Heb.6:8.]] 2. Of persons, rejected after testing, reprobate: [[romans 1 28|Rom.1:28]], [[1-corinthians 9 27|1Co.9:27]], [[2-corinthians 13 5|2Co.13:5-7]], [[2-timothy 3 8|2Ti.3:8]], [[titus 1 16|Tit.1:16]] (Cremer, 212). † (AS)

ἄδολος, -ον, 1. guileless (Pind., Thuc). 2. Of liquids (Æsch., Eur., and late prose writers), genuine, pure (in π. and in MGr. of wine, also of corn: MM, VGT, see word; Milligan, NTD, 77): of milk, metaphorically, [[1-peter 2 2|1Pe.2:2.]] † SYN.: ἀκέραιος (which see), ἄκακος, ἁπλοῦς. (AS)
Ἁδραμυντηνός (T, Rec. Ἀδραμυττηνός), -ή,-όν, of Adramyttium, a seaport of Mysia: [[acts 27 2|Act.27:2.]]† (AS)
Ἁδρίας (T, Rec. Ἀδρίας), -ου, ὁ, the Adriatic sea, in later Greek usage extended to take in all the waters between Greece and Italy: [[acts 27 27|Act.27:27.]]† (AS)
